changes_made.explanation: Normalized task naming, corrected outputs to be more specific, and added the POPE evaluation outputs (Yes/No responses)
Removed CHAIR variants (CHAIR I, CHAIR S) as they are sub-types of CHAIR. Removed POPE as it's an evaluation method/framework, not a metric. Kept base forms of metrics.
No LLMs are used as judges/evaluators in this paper. LVLMs are evaluated but they are the subjects being evaluated, not the evaluators.
The paper uses only automatic evaluation methods (CHAIR, POPE) and does not conduct any human evaluations.

overall_notes: The paper focuses on evaluating object hallucination in Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) using automatic metrics. The main contribution is the POPE (Polling-based Object Probing Evaluation) framework, which converts hallucination evaluation into a binary classification task. All evaluations are automated with no human or LLM-as-judge components.
